6.1 Sport Motivation Scale-2 and BEA validity analysis

Sport Motivation Scale-2 (SMS-2) is used as part of the validity investigation of BEA. SMS-2 consists of 18 items and six sub-scales divided into the following according to Pelletier et al. (2013): Intrinsic regulation (items 3, 9, 17); Integrated regulation (items 4, 11, 14); Identified regulation (items 6, 12, 18); Introjected regulation (items 1, 7, 16); External regulation (items 5, 8, 15); and Amotivated regulation (items 2, 10, 13). These six sub-scales of SMS-2 will be used and analyzed separate with Rasch analysis. Since each sub-scale only contain three items, no (potential) bad performing items will be removed since a subsequent Rasch analysis with only two items would not be meaningful - which should be acknowledged as a limitation prior to the analyses. Validity analyses by correlations of thetas between BEA and each respective SMS-2 sub-scale will then be undertaken. Lastly, partial correlations were conducted to examine the association between BEA and SMS-2 sub-scales, while controlling for the shared variance among the sub-scales. Note that SMS-2 was not completed by the participants from the intervention study (Hockeystudien), therefore more missing values than in the BEA Rasch analysis are to be expected.

6.2 Data preparation

The following data preparations are the basis for all analyses related to the Bulls Eye for Athletes (BEA) study. Code for scale step alterations and some of the modified data frames are presented next to their related sub-analysis to make the workflow more comprehensible.

  • Data preparation

library(eRm)
library(devtools)
library(easyRasch)

library(car)
library(easystats)

bulls_eye_merged_superfinal_data[, ADAQ_adjust] <- lapply(bulls_eye_merged_superfinal_data[, ADAQ_adjust], function(x)
  x - 1)

#SWLS, adjust (-1) to enable Rasch analysis
SWLS_adjust <- c("SWLS.1", "SWLS.2", "SWLS.3", "SWLS.4", "SWLS.5")

bulls_eye_merged_superfinal_data[, SWLS_adjust] <- lapply(bulls_eye_merged_superfinal_data[, SWLS_adjust], function(x)
  x - 1)

#VQ adjustments
#some items were reversed in the scoring when exporting data from the web platform, but no items should be reversed in VQ when using each subscale separately. Some items were therefore reversed back.
#items 1, 2, 6, 8, 10 (the VQ obstruction subscale) were reversed in the scoring and needs to be reversed back.
#VQ already starts at zero and does therefore not need to be adjusted prior to Rasch analysis.

bulls_eye_merged_superfinal_data <- bulls_eye_merged_superfinal_data %>%
  mutate(across(c("VQ.1", "VQ.2", "VQ.6", "VQ.8", "VQ.10"), ~ 6 - .))

#SMS-2 adjustments
#SMS-2 consists of 18 items and 6 sub-scales divided into the following according to Pelletier et al. (2013). Some items were reversed in the scoring when exporting data from the web platform, but no items should be reversed in SMS-2. Some items were therefore reversed back.
#Intrinsic regulation: items 3, 9, 17 (none reversed = correct)
#Integrated regulation: items 4, 11, 14 (none reversed = correct) 
#Identified regulation: items 6, 12, 18 (none reversed = correct)
#Introjected regulation: items 1, 7, 16 (items 1 and 7 are reversed in the scoring and needs to be reversed back)
#External regulation: items 5, 8, 15 (items 5 and 8 are reversed in the scoring and needs to be reversed back)
#Amotivated regulation: 2, 10, 13 (items 2, 10 and 13 are reversed in the scoring and needs to be reversed back)

#(back) reverse scoring for items 1, 7, 5, 8, 2, 10, 13
SMS2_items_to_reverse <- c("SMS_2_1", "SMS_2_7", "SMS_2_5", 
                      "SMS_2_8", "SMS_2_2", "SMS_2_10", "SMS_2_13")

bulls_eye_merged_superfinal_data <- bulls_eye_merged_superfinal_data %>%
  mutate(across(all_of(SMS2_items_to_reverse), ~ 8 - .))

#SMS-2, adjust (-1) to enable Rasch analysis
SMS2_adjust <- c("SMS_2_1",
                 "SMS_2_2",
                 "SMS_2_3",
                 "SMS_2_4",
                 "SMS_2_5",
                 "SMS_2_6",
                 "SMS_2_7",
                 "SMS_2_8",
                 "SMS_2_9",
                 "SMS_2_10",
                 "SMS_2_11",
                 "SMS_2_12",
                 "SMS_2_13",
                 "SMS_2_14",
                 "SMS_2_15",
                 "SMS_2_16",
                 "SMS_2_17",
                 "SMS_2_18"
)

bulls_eye_merged_superfinal_data[, SMS2_adjust] <- lapply(bulls_eye_merged_superfinal_data[, SMS2_adjust], function(x)
  x - 1)

#CSAI-2R adjustments
#CSAI-2R consists of 17 items and 3 sub-scales divided into the following according to Lundqvist & Hassmén (2005). Items will be renamed so they correspond to item numbers in Lundqvist & Hassmén (2005). Some items were reversed in the scoring when exporting data from the web platform (self-confidence sub-scale items), but no items needs to be reversed in CSAI-2R when looking at each sub-scale separately. Items in the self-confidence sub-scale were therefore reversed back.
#items in brackets are the original item numbers found in Lundqvist & Hassmén (2005), items prior to brackets were the item numbers used on the web platform used for data collection in this study
#cognitive anxiety sub-scale: items 2 (7), 5 (10), 7 (13), 9 (16), 13 (22)
#somatic anxiety sub-scale: items 1 (5), 3 (8), 6 (11), 10 (17), 12 (20), 14 (23), 16 (26)
#self-confidence sub-scale: items 4 (9), 8 (15), 11 (18), 15 (24), 17 (27) 

#rename CSAI-2R item names to correspond with Lundqvist & Hassmén (2005):

  "CSAI_2R_1" = "CSAI_2R_5",
  "CSAI_2R_2" = "CSAI_2R_7",
  "CSAI_2R_3" = "CSAI_2R_8",
  "CSAI_2R_4" = "CSAI_2R_9",

  "CSAI_2R_7" = "CSAI_2R_13",
  "CSAI_2R_8" = "CSAI_2R_15",
  "CSAI_2R_9" = "CSAI_2R_16",
  "CSAI_2R_10" = "CSAI_2R_17",
  "CSAI_2R_11" = "CSAI_2R_18",
  "CSAI_2R_12" = "CSAI_2R_20",
  "CSAI_2R_13" = "CSAI_2R_22",
  "CSAI_2R_14" = "CSAI_2R_23",
  "CSAI_2R_15" = "CSAI_2R_24",
  "CSAI_2R_16" = "CSAI_2R_26",
  "CSAI_2R_17" = "CSAI_2R_27"
)

names(bulls_eye_merged_superfinal_data) <- sapply(
  names(bulls_eye_merged_superfinal_data),
  function(x) ifelse(x %in% names(item_mapping_CSAI2R), item_mapping_CSAI2R[x], x)
)

#(back) reverse scoring for self-confidence sub-scale items 9, 15, 18, 24, 27
CSAI2R_items_to_reverse <- c("CSAI_2R_9", "CSAI_2R_15", "CSAI_2R_18", "CSAI_2R_24", "CSAI_2R_27")

bulls_eye_merged_superfinal_data <- bulls_eye_merged_superfinal_data %>%
  mutate(across(all_of(CSAI2R_items_to_reverse), ~ 5 - .))

#CSAI-2R, adjust (-1) to enable Rasch analysis
CSAI2R_adjust <- c(
  "CSAI_2R_5", "CSAI_2R_7", "CSAI_2R_8", "CSAI_2R_9", "CSAI_2R_10", "CSAI_2R_11",

#adding recoded bulls eye items (from the BEA Rasch analysis, needed here as the loading of data needs to be repeated for each quarto file)
recode <- dplyr::recode

bulls_eye_merged_superfinal_data <- bulls_eye_merged_superfinal_data %>%
  mutate(
    # Recoding BE_Competition (0+1; 2+3; 4+5)
    BE_Competition_recoded = recode(
      BE_Competition,
      `0` = 0, `1` = 0,
      `2` = 1, `3` = 1,
      `4` = 2, `5` = 2,
      `6` = 3
    ),
    # Recoding BE_Training (0+1)
    BE_Training_recoded = recode(
      BE_Training,
      `0` = 0, `1` = 0,
      `2` = 1,
      `3` = 2, 
      `4` = 3,
      `5` = 4,
      `6` = 5
    ))

6.3 Intrinsic regulation (SMS-2): Rasch analysis and BEA validity investigation

Rasch analysis of Intrinsic regulation (SMS-2), items 3, 9, 17

Code
itemlabels <- data.frame(itemnr = c("item3", "item9", "item17"),
                         item = c("Because it is very interesting to learn how I can improve.",
                                  "Because I find it enjoyable to discover new performance strategies.",

6.4 Re-analysis of intrinsic_regulation_SMS2 recoded version

Based on the analysis of the response categories and threshold locations, scale steps were merged and recoded so that each kept scale step had the highest response probability at some point on the person location scale, and also so that all threshold locations were in the right order for all items. Recoded items were given new names with the abbreviation “_recoded”.

#add recoded intrinsic_regulation_SMS2

bulls_eye_merged_superfinal_data <- bulls_eye_merged_superfinal_data %>%
  mutate(
    # Recoding SMS_2_3 (0+1, 2+3, 4+5)
    SMS_2_3_recoded = recode(
      SMS_2_3,
      `0` = 0, `1` = 0,
      `2` = 1, `3` = 1,
      `4` = 2, `5` = 2,
      `6` = 3
    ), 
    # Recoding SMS_2_9 (1+2)
    SMS_2_9_recoded = recode(
      SMS_2_9,
      `0` = 0, 
      `1` = 1, `2` = 1, 
      `3` = 2,
      `4` = 3, 
      `5` = 4,
      `6` = 5
    ), 
    # Recoding SMS_2_17 (0+1+2)
    SMS_2_17_recoded = recode(
      SMS_2_17,
      `0` = 0, `1` = 0, `2` = 0, 
      `3` = 1,
      `4` = 2, 
      `5` = 3,
      `6` = 4
    ))

All items are kept anyway for the validity analysis since a Rasch re-analysis with only two items would not be meaningful.

6.5 Intrinsic regulation (SMS2) and BEA validity analysis

Validity between intrinsic_regulation_SMS2 and BEA is investigated by correlation analysis. As both scales has undergone Rasch analysis, participants theta estimates (computed with weighted likelihood estimation - WLE) will be correlated, and since thetas are interval data, Pearson’s correlation is applied.

  • Prepring data
  • Preparing item data frames
  • Outlier identification
  • Correlation intrinsic_regulation_SMS2 and BEA
  • Sensitivity analysis intrinsic_regulation_SMS2 and BEA, time latency

6.7 Re-analysis of integrated_regulation_SMS2 recoded version

Based on the analysis of the response categories and threshold locations, scale steps were merged and recoded so that each kept scale step had the highest response probability at some point on the person location scale, and also so that all threshold locations were in the right order for all items. Recoded items were given new names with the abbreviation “_recoded”.

6.8 Integrated regulation (SMS-2) and BEA validity analysis

Validity between integrated_regulation_SMS2 and BEA is investigated by correlation analysis. As both scales has undergone Rasch analysis, participants theta estimates (computed with weighted likelihood estimation - WLE) will be correlated, and since thetas are interval data, Pearson’s correlation is applied.

  • Prepring data
  • Preparing item data frames
  • Outlier identification
  • Correlation integrated_regulation_SMS2 and BEA
  • Sensitivity analysis integrated_regulation_SMS2 and BEA, time latency
Code
#complete cases data frame for validity analyses

#removing missing values in relevant items for complete cases analysis
#only BE items and one item from the other scales in the bulls eye study
#is needed (in this case the SubjektivPrestation item) 
#this is because there are no missing values for the other scales 
#after the intervention study (Hockeystudien) participants have been removed
#therefore this data frame will work for all validity analyses 

items_validity_analyses <- c(
  "BE_Competition_recoded",
  "BE_Training_recoded",
  "BE_PreparationRecovery",
  "BE_Life",
  "SubjektivPrestation"
)

data_complete_cases <- bulls_eye_merged_superfinal_data[complete.cases(bulls_eye_merged_superfinal_data[, items_validity_analyses]), ]

#155 participants to begin with
#33 participants from the intervention study (Hockeystudien) were removed (did not complete any scale beside Bulls Eye)
#1 participant (not from the intervention study) who completed the other scales but not the dartboard in Bulls Eye (only other parts of BE) and were therefore removed
#results in a complete cases data frame with 121 participants 

nrow(data_complete_cases)
[1] 121
Code
#item data frames
BE_validity_analyses <- data_complete_cases[, c(
  "BE_Competition_recoded",
  "BE_Training_recoded",
  "BE_PreparationRecovery",
  "BE_Life"
)]

integrated_regulation_SMS2_validity_analyses <- data_complete_cases[, c(
  "SMS_2_4_recoded",
  "SMS_2_11_recoded",
  "SMS_2_14_recoded"
)]

#extracting thetas
BE_thetas <- RIestThetas(BE_validity_analyses)

integrated_regulation_SMS2_thetas <- RIestThetas(integrated_regulation_SMS2_validity_analyses)

#adding thetas to the data frame
data_complete_cases$BE_thetas_WLE <- BE_thetas$WLE 
data_complete_cases$integrated_regulation_SMS2_thetas_WLE <- integrated_regulation_SMS2_thetas$WLE

Visual inspection of potential outliers was only conducted for BEA to have the same sub-sample across validity correlation analyses. One statistical outlier was detected and marked in red in the plot below. This participant was row 28 in the data frame and will be removed in the upcoming correlation.

{

}

)

  mutate(group = factor(ifelse(time_latency_survey1_bulls_eye1_days < 1,"same_day","different_day")))

anova(m0_integrated_regulation_SMS2, m1_integrated_regulation_SMS2)

6.10 Re-analysis of identified_regulation_SMS2 recoded version

Based on the analysis of the response categories and threshold locations, scale steps were merged and recoded so that each kept scale step had the highest response probability at some point on the person location scale, and also so that all threshold locations were in the right order for all items. Recoded items were given new names with the abbreviation “_recoded”.

6.11 Identified regulation (SMS-2) and BEA validity analysis

Validity between identified_regulation_SMS2 and BEA is investigated by correlation analysis. As both scales has undergone Rasch analysis, participants theta estimates (computed with weighted likelihood estimation - WLE) will be correlated, and since thetas are interval data, Pearson’s correlation is applied.

  • Prepring data
  • Preparing item data frames
  • Outlier identification
  • Correlation identified_regulation_SMS2 and BEA
  • Sensitivity analysis identified_regulation_SMS2 and BEA, time latency
Code
#complete cases data frame for validity analyses

#removing missing values in relevant items for complete cases analysis
#only BE items and one item from the other scales in the bulls eye study
#is needed (in this case the SubjektivPrestation item) 
#this is because there are no missing values for the other scales 
#after the intervention study (Hockeystudien) participants have been removed
#therefore this data frame will work for all validity analyses 

items_validity_analyses <- c(
  "BE_Competition_recoded",
  "BE_Training_recoded",
  "BE_PreparationRecovery",
  "BE_Life",
  "SubjektivPrestation"
)

data_complete_cases <- bulls_eye_merged_superfinal_data[complete.cases(bulls_eye_merged_superfinal_data[, items_validity_analyses]), ]

#155 participants to begin with
#33 participants from the intervention study (Hockeystudien) were removed (did not complete any scale beside Bulls Eye)
#1 participant (not from the intervention study) who completed the other scales but not the dartboard in Bulls Eye (only other parts of BE) and were therefore removed
#results in a complete cases data frame with 121 participants 

nrow(data_complete_cases)
[1] 121

  "BE_Life"
)]

)]

#extracting thetas
BE_thetas <- RIestThetas(BE_validity_analyses)

identified_regulation_SMS2_thetas <- RIestThetas(identified_regulation_SMS2_validity_analyses)

#adding thetas to the data frame
data_complete_cases$BE_thetas_WLE <- BE_thetas$WLE
data_complete_cases$identified_regulation_SMS2_thetas_WLE <- identified_regulation_SMS2_thetas$WLE

6.13 Re-analysis of introjected_regulation_SMS2 recoded version

Based on the analysis of the response categories and threshold locations, scale steps were merged and recoded so that each kept scale step had the highest response probability at some point on the person location scale, and also so that all threshold locations were in the right order for all items. Recoded items were given new names with the abbreviation “_recoded”.

6.14 Introjected regulation (SMS-2) and BEA validity analysis

Validity between introjected_regulation_SMS2 and BEA is investigated by correlation analysis. As both scales has undergone Rasch analysis, participants theta estimates (computed with weighted likelihood estimation - WLE) will be correlated, and since thetas are interval data, Pearson’s correlation is applied.

  • Prepring data
  • Preparing item data frames
  • Outlier identification
  • Correlation introjected_regulation_SMS2 and BEA
  • Sensitivity analysis introjected_regulation_SMS2 and BEA, time latency

data_complete_cases <- bulls_eye_merged_superfinal_data[complete.cases(bulls_eye_merged_superfinal_data[, items_validity_analyses]), ]

6.16 Re-analysis of external_regulation_SMS2 recoded version

Based on the analysis of the response categories and threshold locations, scale steps were merged and recoded so that each kept scale step had the highest response probability at some point on the person location scale, and also so that all threshold locations were in the right order for all items. Recoded items were given new names with the abbreviation “_recoded”.

6.17 External regulation (SMS-2) and BEA validity analysis

Validity between external_regulation_SMS2 and BEA is investigated by correlation analysis. As both scales has undergone Rasch analysis, participants theta estimates (computed with weighted likelihood estimation - WLE) will be correlated, and since thetas are interval data, Pearson’s correlation is applied.

  • Prepring data
  • Preparing item data frames
  • Outlier identification
  • Correlation external_regulation_SMS2 and BEA
  • Sensitivity analysis external_regulation_SMS2 and BEA, time latency
Code
#complete cases data frame for validity analyses

#removing missing values in relevant items for complete cases analysis
#only BE items and one item from the other scales in the bulls eye study
#is needed (in this case the SubjektivPrestation item) 
#this is because there are no missing values for the other scales 
#after the intervention study (Hockeystudien) participants have been removed
#therefore this data frame will work for all validity analyses 

items_validity_analyses <- c(
  "BE_Competition_recoded",
  "BE_Training_recoded",
  "BE_PreparationRecovery",
  "BE_Life",
  "SubjektivPrestation"

data_complete_cases <- bulls_eye_merged_superfinal_data[complete.cases(bulls_eye_merged_superfinal_data[, items_validity_analyses]), ]

#155 participants to begin with

#we can also check if there is a statistically significant difference

  mutate(group = factor(ifelse(time_latency_survey1_bulls_eye1_days < 1,"same_day","different_day")))

anova(m0_external_regulation_SMS2, m1_external_regulation_SMS2)

6.19 Re-analysis of amotivated_regulation_SMS2 recoded version

Based on the analysis of the response categories and threshold locations, scale steps were merged and recoded so that each kept scale step had the highest response probability at some point on the person location scale, and also so that all threshold locations were in the right order for all items. Recoded items were given new names with the abbreviation “_recoded”.

6.20 Amotivated regulation (SMS-2) and BEA validity analysis

Validity between amotivated_regulation_SMS2 and BEA is investigated by correlation analysis. As both scales has undergone Rasch analysis, participants theta estimates (computed with weighted likelihood estimation - WLE) will be correlated, and since thetas are interval data, Pearson’s correlation is applied.

  • Prepring data
  • Preparing item data frames
  • Outlier identification
  • Correlation amotivated_regulation_SMS2 and BEA
  • Sensitivity analysis amotivated_regulation_SMS2 and BEA, time latency

#complete cases data frame for validity analyses

#removing missing values in relevant items for complete cases analysis
#only BE items and one item from the other scales in the bulls eye study
#is needed (in this case the SubjektivPrestation item) 
#this is because there are no missing values for the other scales 
#after the intervention study (Hockeystudien) participants have been removed
#therefore this data frame will work for all validity analyses 

items_validity_analyses <- c(
  "BE_Competition_recoded",
  "BE_Training_recoded",
  "BE_PreparationRecovery",
  "BE_Life",
  "SubjektivPrestation"
)

## Sport Motivation Scale-2 and BEA validity analysis
Sport Motivation Scale-2 (SMS-2) is used as part of the validity investigation of BEA. SMS-2 consists of 18 items and six sub-scales divided into the following according to Pelletier et al. (2013): Intrinsic regulation (items 3, 9, 17); Integrated regulation (items 4, 11, 14); Identified regulation (items 6, 12, 18); Introjected regulation (items 1, 7, 16); External regulation (items 5, 8, 15); and Amotivated regulation (items 2, 10, 13). These six sub-scales of SMS-2 will be used and analyzed separate with Rasch analysis. Since each sub-scale only contain three items, no (potential) bad performing items will be removed since a subsequent Rasch analysis with only two items would not be meaningful - which should be acknowledged as a limitation prior to the analyses. Validity analyses by correlations of thetas between BEA and each respective SMS-2 sub-scale will then be undertaken. Lastly, partial correlations were conducted to examine the association between BEA and SMS-2 sub-scales, while controlling for the shared variance among the sub-scales. Note that SMS-2 was not completed by the participants from the intervention study (Hockeystudien), therefore more missing values than in the BEA Rasch analysis are to be expected.

```{r}
itemlabels <- data.frame(itemnr = paste0("item",1:18),
                         item = c("Because I would feel bad about myself if I did not take the time to do it.",
                                  "I used to have good reasons for doing sports, but now I am asking myself if I should continue.",
                                  "Because it is very interesting to learn how I can improve.",
                                  "Because practicing sports reflects the essence of whom I am.",
                                  "Because people I care about would be upset with me if I didn’t.",
                                  "Because I found it is a good way to develop aspects of myself that I value.",
                                  "Because I would not feel worthwhile if I did not.",
                                  "Because I think others would disapprove of me if I did not.",
                                  "Because I find it enjoyable to discover new performance strategies.",
                                  "I don’t know anymore; I have the impression that I am incapable of succeeding in this sport.",
                                  "Because participating in sport is an integral part of my life.",
                                  "Because I have chosen this sport as a way to develop myself.",
                                  "It is not clear to me anymore; I don’t really think my place is in sport.",
                                  "Because through sport, I am living in line with my deepest principles.",
                                  "Because people around me reward me when I do.",
                                  "Because I feel better about myself when I do.",
                                  "Because it gives me pleasure to learn more about my sport.",
                                  "Because it is one of the best ways I have chosen to develop other aspects of myself."))


RIlistitems(itemlabels, all.items = TRUE)
```


## Data preparation

The following data preparations are the basis for all analyses related to the Bulls Eye for Athletes (BEA) study. Code for scale step alterations and some of the modified data frames are presented next to their related sub-analysis to make the workflow more comprehensible.

::: panel-tabset

### R packages

```{r}
#| label: R packages 
#| echo: true

library(readxl)
library(tidyverse)
library(eRm)
library(devtools)
library(easyRasch)
library(iarm)
library(mirt)
library(conflicted)
library(car)
library(easystats)
```

hockeystudien_intervention_demographics$Demografi.Alder[hockeystudien_intervention_demographics$Användarnamn == "1077dhrv" &
                                                          hockeystudien_intervention_demographics$Demografi.Alder == 6] <- 26


#merge df BE and demographics from hockeystudien
merged_data_hockeystudien_BE_demographics <- full_join(merged_data_hockeystudien_BE,
                                                       hockeystudien_intervention_demographics,
                                                       by = "Användarnamn")

#following in the hockeystudien study already exists in the bulls eye study, therefore mask:
#mask 1029spns, 1061bgmb, 1043gsnq, 1046pkbz, 1062xhqd, 1070mfqq
#1073znwk is also masked due to not completing the dart board ratings in BEA (only other parts of BEA) and therefore not contributing with any values for the statistical analyses

usernames_to_exclude <- c("1029spns",
                          "1061bgmb",
                          "1043gsnq",
                          "1046pkbz",
                          "1062xhqd",
                          "1070mfqq",
                          "1073znwk")

filtered_data <- merged_data_hockeystudien_BE_demographics %>%
  filter(!(`Användarnamn` %in% usernames_to_exclude))


hockeystudien_bulls_eye_modified_data <- filtered_data %>%
  mutate(`Användarnamn` = paste0(`Användarnamn`, "_hockeystudien")) %>%  # Append "_hockeystudien" to each value
  rename(
    BE_Competition = Tavling,
    BE_Training = Traning,
    BE_PreparationRecovery = Forberedelser,
    BE_Life = Livet,
    BE_Obstacles_Sport = HinderSkala1,
    BE_Obstacles_Life = HinderSkala2
  )




#preparations for merging datasets into superfinal version (bulls eye + hockeystudien_bulls eye)

hockeystudien_bulls_eye_modified_data <- hockeystudien_bulls_eye_modified_data %>%
  mutate(from_hockeystudien = 1)

BullsEye_merged_data_final <- BullsEye_merged_data_final %>%
  mutate(from_hockeystudien = 0)

bulls_eye_merged_superfinal_data <- bind_rows(hockeystudien_bulls_eye_modified_data,
                                              BullsEye_merged_data_final) #use for analyses

#BE items (dartboard), adjust (-1) to enable Rasch analysis
BE_adjust <- c(
  "BE_Competition",
  "BE_Training",
  "BE_PreparationRecovery",
  "BE_Life",
  "BE_Competition_test2",
  "BE_Training_test2",
  "BE_PreparationRecovery_test2",
  "BE_Life_test2"
)

bulls_eye_merged_superfinal_data[, BE_adjust] <- lapply(bulls_eye_merged_superfinal_data[, BE_adjust], function(x)
  x - 1)

#"Hinder", reverse items (low value = low in values-based living and compatible with other values items) and adjust (-1) to enable Rasch analysis
Hinder_reverse_and_adjust <- c(
  "BE_Obstacles_Sport",
  "BE_Obstacles_Life",
  "BE_Obstacles_Sport_test2",
  "BE_Obstacles_Life_test2"
)

bulls_eye_merged_superfinal_data[, Hinder_reverse_and_adjust] <- lapply(bulls_eye_merged_superfinal_data[, Hinder_reverse_and_adjust], function(x)
  8 - x - 1)

#ADAQ, adjust (-1) to enable Rasch analysis
ADAQ_adjust <- c("ADAQ.1",
                 "ADAQ.2",
                 "ADAQ.3",
                 "ADAQ.4",
                 "ADAQ.5",
                 "ADAQ.6",
                 "ADAQ.7")

bulls_eye_merged_superfinal_data[, ADAQ_adjust] <- lapply(bulls_eye_merged_superfinal_data[, ADAQ_adjust], function(x)
  x - 1)

#SWLS, adjust (-1) to enable Rasch analysis
SWLS_adjust <- c("SWLS.1", "SWLS.2", "SWLS.3", "SWLS.4", "SWLS.5")

bulls_eye_merged_superfinal_data[, SWLS_adjust] <- lapply(bulls_eye_merged_superfinal_data[, SWLS_adjust], function(x)
  x - 1)

#VQ adjustments
#some items were reversed in the scoring when exporting data from the web platform, but no items should be reversed in VQ when using each subscale separately. Some items were therefore reversed back.
#items 1, 2, 6, 8, 10 (the VQ obstruction subscale) were reversed in the scoring and needs to be reversed back.
#VQ already starts at zero and does therefore not need to be adjusted prior to Rasch analysis.

bulls_eye_merged_superfinal_data <- bulls_eye_merged_superfinal_data %>%
  mutate(across(c("VQ.1", "VQ.2", "VQ.6", "VQ.8", "VQ.10"), ~ 6 - .))

#SMS-2 adjustments
#SMS-2 consists of 18 items and 6 sub-scales divided into the following according to Pelletier et al. (2013). Some items were reversed in the scoring when exporting data from the web platform, but no items should be reversed in SMS-2. Some items were therefore reversed back.
#Intrinsic regulation: items 3, 9, 17 (none reversed = correct)
#Integrated regulation: items 4, 11, 14 (none reversed = correct) 
#Identified regulation: items 6, 12, 18 (none reversed = correct)
#Introjected regulation: items 1, 7, 16 (items 1 and 7 are reversed in the scoring and needs to be reversed back)
#External regulation: items 5, 8, 15 (items 5 and 8 are reversed in the scoring and needs to be reversed back)
#Amotivated regulation: 2, 10, 13 (items 2, 10 and 13 are reversed in the scoring and needs to be reversed back)

#(back) reverse scoring for items 1, 7, 5, 8, 2, 10, 13
SMS2_items_to_reverse <- c("SMS_2_1", "SMS_2_7", "SMS_2_5", 
                      "SMS_2_8", "SMS_2_2", "SMS_2_10", "SMS_2_13")

bulls_eye_merged_superfinal_data <- bulls_eye_merged_superfinal_data %>%
  mutate(across(all_of(SMS2_items_to_reverse), ~ 8 - .))

#SMS-2, adjust (-1) to enable Rasch analysis
SMS2_adjust <- c("SMS_2_1",
                 "SMS_2_2",
                 "SMS_2_3",
                 "SMS_2_4",
                 "SMS_2_5",
                 "SMS_2_6",
                 "SMS_2_7",
                 "SMS_2_8",
                 "SMS_2_9",
                 "SMS_2_10",
                 "SMS_2_11",
                 "SMS_2_12",
                 "SMS_2_13",
                 "SMS_2_14",
                 "SMS_2_15",
                 "SMS_2_16",
                 "SMS_2_17",
                 "SMS_2_18"
)

bulls_eye_merged_superfinal_data[, SMS2_adjust] <- lapply(bulls_eye_merged_superfinal_data[, SMS2_adjust], function(x)
  x - 1)

#CSAI-2R adjustments
#CSAI-2R consists of 17 items and 3 sub-scales divided into the following according to Lundqvist & Hassmén (2005). Items will be renamed so they correspond to item numbers in Lundqvist & Hassmén (2005). Some items were reversed in the scoring when exporting data from the web platform (self-confidence sub-scale items), but no items needs to be reversed in CSAI-2R when looking at each sub-scale separately. Items in the self-confidence sub-scale were therefore reversed back.
#items in brackets are the original item numbers found in Lundqvist & Hassmén (2005), items prior to brackets were the item numbers used on the web platform used for data collection in this study
#cognitive anxiety sub-scale: items 2 (7), 5 (10), 7 (13), 9 (16), 13 (22)
#somatic anxiety sub-scale: items 1 (5), 3 (8), 6 (11), 10 (17), 12 (20), 14 (23), 16 (26)
#self-confidence sub-scale: items 4 (9), 8 (15), 11 (18), 15 (24), 17 (27) 

#rename CSAI-2R item names to correspond with Lundqvist & Hassmén (2005):
item_mapping_CSAI2R <- c(
  "CSAI_2R_1" = "CSAI_2R_5",
  "CSAI_2R_2" = "CSAI_2R_7",
  "CSAI_2R_3" = "CSAI_2R_8",
  "CSAI_2R_4" = "CSAI_2R_9",
  "CSAI_2R_5" = "CSAI_2R_10",
  "CSAI_2R_6" = "CSAI_2R_11",
  "CSAI_2R_7" = "CSAI_2R_13",
  "CSAI_2R_8" = "CSAI_2R_15",
  "CSAI_2R_9" = "CSAI_2R_16",
  "CSAI_2R_10" = "CSAI_2R_17",
  "CSAI_2R_11" = "CSAI_2R_18",
  "CSAI_2R_12" = "CSAI_2R_20",
  "CSAI_2R_13" = "CSAI_2R_22",
  "CSAI_2R_14" = "CSAI_2R_23",
  "CSAI_2R_15" = "CSAI_2R_24",
  "CSAI_2R_16" = "CSAI_2R_26",
  "CSAI_2R_17" = "CSAI_2R_27"
)

names(bulls_eye_merged_superfinal_data) <- sapply(
  names(bulls_eye_merged_superfinal_data),
  function(x) ifelse(x %in% names(item_mapping_CSAI2R), item_mapping_CSAI2R[x], x)
)

#(back) reverse scoring for self-confidence sub-scale items 9, 15, 18, 24, 27
CSAI2R_items_to_reverse <- c("CSAI_2R_9", "CSAI_2R_15", "CSAI_2R_18", "CSAI_2R_24", "CSAI_2R_27")

bulls_eye_merged_superfinal_data <- bulls_eye_merged_superfinal_data %>%
  mutate(across(all_of(CSAI2R_items_to_reverse), ~ 5 - .))

#CSAI-2R, adjust (-1) to enable Rasch analysis
CSAI2R_adjust <- c(
  "CSAI_2R_5", "CSAI_2R_7", "CSAI_2R_8", "CSAI_2R_9", "CSAI_2R_10", "CSAI_2R_11",
  "CSAI_2R_13", "CSAI_2R_15", "CSAI_2R_16", "CSAI_2R_17", "CSAI_2R_18", "CSAI_2R_20",
  "CSAI_2R_22", "CSAI_2R_23", "CSAI_2R_24", "CSAI_2R_26", "CSAI_2R_27"
)

bulls_eye_merged_superfinal_data[, CSAI2R_adjust] <- lapply(
  bulls_eye_merged_superfinal_data[, CSAI2R_adjust],
  function(x) x - 1
)

#adding recoded bulls eye items (from the BEA Rasch analysis, needed here as the loading of data needs to be repeated for each quarto file)
recode <- dplyr::recode

bulls_eye_merged_superfinal_data <- bulls_eye_merged_superfinal_data %>%
  mutate(
    # Recoding BE_Competition (0+1; 2+3; 4+5)
    BE_Competition_recoded = recode(
      BE_Competition,
      `0` = 0, `1` = 0,
      `2` = 1, `3` = 1,
      `4` = 2, `5` = 2,
      `6` = 3
    ),
    # Recoding BE_Training (0+1)
    BE_Training_recoded = recode(
      BE_Training,
      `0` = 0, `1` = 0,
      `2` = 1,
      `3` = 2, 
      `4` = 3,
      `5` = 4,
      `6` = 5
    ))

```

```{r}

                         item = c("Because it is very interesting to learn how I can improve.",

## Re-analysis of intrinsic_regulation_SMS2 recoded version 

Based on the analysis of the response categories and threshold locations, scale steps were merged and recoded so that each kept scale step had the highest response probability at some point on the person location scale, and also so that all threshold locations were in the right order for all items. Recoded items were given new names with the abbreviation "_recoded". 

::: panel-tabset

      `2` = 1, `3` = 1,

      `0` = 0, 
      `1` = 1, `2` = 1, 
      `3` = 2,
      `4` = 3, 
      `5` = 4,
      `6` = 5

    # Recoding SMS_2_17 (0+1+2)

All items are kept anyway for the validity analysis since a Rasch re-analysis with only two items would not be meaningful. 

## Intrinsic regulation (SMS2) and BEA validity analysis
Validity between intrinsic_regulation_SMS2 and BEA is investigated by correlation analysis. As both scales has undergone Rasch analysis, participants theta estimates (computed with weighted likelihood estimation - WLE) will be correlated, and since thetas are interval data, Pearson's correlation is applied.

::: panel-tabset

### Prepring data

```{r}
#complete cases data frame for validity analyses

#removing missing values in relevant items for complete cases analysis
#only BE items and one item from the other scales in the bulls eye study
#is needed (in this case the SubjektivPrestation item) 
#this is because there are no missing values for the other scales 
#after the intervention study (Hockeystudien) participants have been removed
#therefore this data frame will work for all validity analyses 

items_validity_analyses <- c(
  "BE_Competition_recoded",
  "BE_Training_recoded",
  "BE_PreparationRecovery",
  "BE_Life",
  "SubjektivPrestation"
)

data_complete_cases <- bulls_eye_merged_superfinal_data[complete.cases(bulls_eye_merged_superfinal_data[, items_validity_analyses]), ]

#155 participants to begin with
#33 participants from the intervention study (Hockeystudien) were removed (did not complete any scale beside Bulls Eye)
#1 participant (not from the intervention study) who completed the other scales but not the dartboard in Bulls Eye (only other parts of BE) and were therefore removed
#results in a complete cases data frame with 121 participants 

nrow(data_complete_cases)
```

### Preparing item data frames

```{r}
#item data frames
BE_validity_analyses <- data_complete_cases[, c(
  "BE_Competition_recoded",
  "BE_Training_recoded",
  "BE_PreparationRecovery",
  "BE_Life"
)]

intrinsic_regulation_SMS2_validity_analyses <- data_complete_cases[, c(
  "SMS_2_3_recoded",
  "SMS_2_9_recoded",
  "SMS_2_17_recoded"
)]

#extracting thetas

)

### Sensitivity analysis intrinsic_regulation_SMS2 and BEA, time latency
Some participants did not complete BEA and SMS-2 during the same day as intended. Therefore, a sensitivity analysis is conducted.

```{r}
#creating data frame with only participants that completed Bulls Eye and the other scales during the same day
#since 17 participants did not (has already been checked in a prior validity analysis), 104 participants will remain 
data_complete_cases_less_than_1day <- subset(data_complete_cases, time_latency_survey1_bulls_eye1_days < 1)
```

```{r}
#looking only at participants who completed Bulls Eye and the other scales during the same day (N = 104)

#sensitivity analysis intrinsic_regulation_SMS2 and BE
BE_validity_analyses_less1day <- data_complete_cases_less_than_1day[, c(
  "BE_Competition_recoded",
  "BE_Training_recoded",
  "BE_PreparationRecovery",
  "BE_Life"
)]

intrinsic_regulation_SMS2_validity_analyses_less1day <- data_complete_cases_less_than_1day[, c(
  "SMS_2_3_recoded",
  "SMS_2_9_recoded",
  "SMS_2_17_recoded"
)]

#extracting thetas
BE_thetas_less1day <- RIestThetas(BE_validity_analyses_less1day)

intrinsic_regulation_SMS2_thetas_less1day <- RIestThetas(intrinsic_regulation_SMS2_validity_analyses_less1day)

#adding thetas to the data frame
data_complete_cases_less_than_1day$BE_thetas_less1day_WLE <- BE_thetas_less1day$WLE

data_complete_cases_less_than_1day$intrinsic_regulation_SMS2_thetas_less1day_WLE <- intrinsic_regulation_SMS2_thetas_less1day$WLE

#analysis only with participants completing Bulls Eye and SMS-2 the same day
#removing the outlier, now on row 20 in the data frame
correlation_BE_intrinsic_regulation_SMS2_less1day <- cor_test(
  data_complete_cases_less_than_1day[-20, ],
  x = "BE_thetas_less1day_WLE",
  y = "intrinsic_regulation_SMS2_thetas_less1day_WLE",
  method = "pearson"
)

print(correlation_BE_intrinsic_regulation_SMS2_less1day)
```

```{r}
#we can also check if there is a statistically significant difference 
#by adding same or different day as a predictor 
#the outlier on row 28 in the data frame is removed
data_complete_cases_sensitivity_analysis <- data_complete_cases %>% 
  mutate(group = factor(ifelse(time_latency_survey1_bulls_eye1_days < 1,"same_day","different_day")))

m0_intrinsic_regulation_SMS2 <- lm(intrinsic_regulation_SMS2_thetas_WLE ~ BE_thetas_WLE, data = data_complete_cases_sensitivity_analysis[-28, ])

m1_intrinsic_regulation_SMS2 <- lm(intrinsic_regulation_SMS2_thetas_WLE ~ BE_thetas_WLE + group, data = data_complete_cases_sensitivity_analysis[-28, ])

anova(m0_intrinsic_regulation_SMS2, m1_intrinsic_regulation_SMS2)
```

Adding whether BE and intrinsic_regulation_SMS2 were completed during the same day or not as a predictor did not significantly alter the results.

## Re-analysis of integrated_regulation_SMS2 recoded version 

Based on the analysis of the response categories and threshold locations, scale steps were merged and recoded so that each kept scale step had the highest response probability at some point on the person location scale, and also so that all threshold locations were in the right order for all items. Recoded items were given new names with the abbreviation "_recoded". 

::: panel-tabset

### Recoding response categories for integrated_regulation_SMS2

```{r}
#add recoded integrated_regulation_SMS2 items

bulls_eye_merged_superfinal_data <- bulls_eye_merged_superfinal_data %>%
  mutate(
    # Recoding SMS_2_4 (1+2)
    SMS_2_4_recoded = recode(
      SMS_2_4,
      `0` = 0, 
      `1` = 1, `2` = 1, 
      `3` = 2,
      `4` = 3, 
      `5` = 4,
      `6` = 5
    ), 
    # Recoding SMS_2_11_revised (1+2)
    SMS_2_11_recoded = recode(
      SMS_2_11_revised,
      `0` = 0, 
      `1` = 1, `2` = 1, 
      `3` = 2,
      `4` = 3
    ),
    # Recoding SMS_2_14 (0+1)
    SMS_2_14_recoded = recode(
      SMS_2_14,
      `0` = 0, `1` = 0, 
      `2` = 1, 
      `3` = 2,
      `4` = 3, 
      `5` = 4,
      `6` = 5
    ))


```

## Integrated regulation (SMS-2) and BEA validity analysis
Validity between integrated_regulation_SMS2 and BEA is investigated by correlation analysis. As both scales has undergone Rasch analysis, participants theta estimates (computed with weighted likelihood estimation - WLE) will be correlated, and since thetas are interval data, Pearson's correlation is applied.

::: panel-tabset

### Prepring data

```{r}
#complete cases data frame for validity analyses

#removing missing values in relevant items for complete cases analysis
#only BE items and one item from the other scales in the bulls eye study
#is needed (in this case the SubjektivPrestation item) 
#this is because there are no missing values for the other scales 
#after the intervention study (Hockeystudien) participants have been removed
#therefore this data frame will work for all validity analyses 

items_validity_analyses <- c(
  "BE_Competition_recoded",
  "BE_Training_recoded",
  "BE_PreparationRecovery",
  "BE_Life",
  "SubjektivPrestation"
)

data_complete_cases <- bulls_eye_merged_superfinal_data[complete.cases(bulls_eye_merged_superfinal_data[, items_validity_analyses]), ]

#155 participants to begin with
#33 participants from the intervention study (Hockeystudien) were removed (did not complete any scale beside Bulls Eye)
#1 participant (not from the intervention study) who completed the other scales but not the dartboard in Bulls Eye (only other parts of BE) and were therefore removed
#results in a complete cases data frame with 121 participants 

nrow(data_complete_cases)
```

#adding thetas to the data frame
data_complete_cases$BE_thetas_WLE <- BE_thetas$WLE 
data_complete_cases$integrated_regulation_SMS2_thetas_WLE <- integrated_regulation_SMS2_thetas$WLE

## Re-analysis of identified_regulation_SMS2 recoded version 

Based on the analysis of the response categories and threshold locations, scale steps were merged and recoded so that each kept scale step had the highest response probability at some point on the person location scale, and also so that all threshold locations were in the right order for all items. Recoded items were given new names with the abbreviation "_recoded".

      `0` = 0, `1` = 0, 
      `2` = 1,

## Identified regulation (SMS-2) and BEA validity analysis
Validity between identified_regulation_SMS2 and BEA is investigated by correlation analysis. As both scales has undergone Rasch analysis, participants theta estimates (computed with weighted likelihood estimation - WLE) will be correlated, and since thetas are interval data, Pearson's correlation is applied.

::: panel-tabset

### Prepring data

```{r}
#complete cases data frame for validity analyses

#removing missing values in relevant items for complete cases analysis
#only BE items and one item from the other scales in the bulls eye study
#is needed (in this case the SubjektivPrestation item) 
#this is because there are no missing values for the other scales 
#after the intervention study (Hockeystudien) participants have been removed
#therefore this data frame will work for all validity analyses 

items_validity_analyses <- c(
  "BE_Competition_recoded",
  "BE_Training_recoded",
  "BE_PreparationRecovery",
  "BE_Life",
  "SubjektivPrestation"
)

data_complete_cases <- bulls_eye_merged_superfinal_data[complete.cases(bulls_eye_merged_superfinal_data[, items_validity_analyses]), ]

#155 participants to begin with
#33 participants from the intervention study (Hockeystudien) were removed (did not complete any scale beside Bulls Eye)
#1 participant (not from the intervention study) who completed the other scales but not the dartboard in Bulls Eye (only other parts of BE) and were therefore removed
#results in a complete cases data frame with 121 participants 

nrow(data_complete_cases)
```

### Preparing item data frames

```{r}
#item data frames
BE_validity_analyses <- data_complete_cases[, c(
  "BE_Competition_recoded",
  "BE_Training_recoded",
  "BE_PreparationRecovery",
  "BE_Life"
)]

identified_regulation_SMS2_validity_analyses <- data_complete_cases[, c(
  "SMS_2_6",
  "SMS_2_12_recoded",
  "SMS_2_18_recoded"
)]

#extracting thetas
BE_thetas <- RIestThetas(BE_validity_analyses)

identified_regulation_SMS2_thetas <- RIestThetas(identified_regulation_SMS2_validity_analyses)

#adding thetas to the data frame
data_complete_cases$BE_thetas_WLE <- BE_thetas$WLE
data_complete_cases$identified_regulation_SMS2_thetas_WLE <- identified_regulation_SMS2_thetas$WLE
```

### Outlier identification
Visual inspection of potential outliers was only conducted for BEA to have the same sub-sample across validity correlation analyses. One statistical outlier was detected and marked in red in the plot below. This participant was row 28 in the data frame and will be removed in the upcoming correlation.

```{r}
{
  plot(data_complete_cases$BE_thetas_WLE,
       main = "Index Plot of BE_thetas_WLE",
       ylab = "BE Theta",
       xlab = "Participant Index",
       pch = 20)
  abline(h = mean(data_complete_cases$BE_thetas_WLE), col = "blue", lty = 2)
  points(28, data_complete_cases$BE_thetas_WLE[28], col = "red", pch = 19)
}
```

### Correlation identified_regulation_SMS2 and BEA

```{r}
#participant on row 28 is an outlier and therefore removed
correlation_BE_identified_regulation_SMS2 <- cor_test(
  data_complete_cases[-28, ],
  x = "BE_thetas_WLE",
  y = "identified_regulation_SMS2_thetas_WLE",
  method = "pearson"
)

print(correlation_BE_identified_regulation_SMS2)

plot(correlation_BE_identified_regulation_SMS2)
```

### Sensitivity analysis identified_regulation_SMS2 and BEA, time latency
Some participants did not complete BEA and SMS-2 during the same day as intended. Therefore, a sensitivity analysis is conducted.

```{r}
#creating data frame with only participants that completed Bulls Eye and the other scales during the same day
#since 17 participants did not (has already been checked in a prior validity analysis), 104 participants will remain 
data_complete_cases_less_than_1day <- subset(data_complete_cases, time_latency_survey1_bulls_eye1_days < 1)
```

```{r}
#looking only at participants who completed Bulls Eye and the other scales during the same day (N = 104)

#sensitivity analysis identified_regulation_SMS2 and BE
BE_validity_analyses_less1day <- data_complete_cases_less_than_1day[, c(
  "BE_Competition_recoded",
  "BE_Training_recoded",
  "BE_PreparationRecovery",
  "BE_Life"
)]

identified_regulation_SMS2_validity_analyses_less1day <- data_complete_cases_less_than_1day[, c(
  "SMS_2_6",
  "SMS_2_12_recoded",
  "SMS_2_18_recoded"
)]

#extracting thetas
BE_thetas_less1day <- RIestThetas(BE_validity_analyses_less1day)

identified_regulation_SMS2_thetas_less1day <- RIestThetas(identified_regulation_SMS2_validity_analyses_less1day)

#adding thetas to the data frame
data_complete_cases_less_than_1day$BE_thetas_less1day_WLE <- BE_thetas_less1day$WLE

data_complete_cases_less_than_1day$identified_regulation_SMS2_thetas_less1day_WLE <- identified_regulation_SMS2_thetas_less1day$WLE

#analysis only with participants completing Bulls Eye and SMS-2 the same day
#removing the outlier, now on row 20 in the data frame
correlation_BE_identified_regulation_SMS2_less1day <- cor_test(
  data_complete_cases_less_than_1day[-20, ],
  x = "BE_thetas_less1day_WLE",
  y = "identified_regulation_SMS2_thetas_less1day_WLE",
  method = "pearson"
)

print(correlation_BE_identified_regulation_SMS2_less1day)
```

```{r}
#we can also check if there is a statistically significant difference 
#by adding same or different day as a predictor
#the outlier on row 28 in the data frame is removed
data_complete_cases_sensitivity_analysis <- data_complete_cases %>% 
  mutate(group = factor(ifelse(time_latency_survey1_bulls_eye1_days < 1,"same_day","different_day")))

m0_identified_regulation_SMS2 <- lm(identified_regulation_SMS2_thetas_WLE ~ BE_thetas_WLE, data = data_complete_cases_sensitivity_analysis[-28, ])

m1_identified_regulation_SMS2 <- lm(identified_regulation_SMS2_thetas_WLE ~ BE_thetas_WLE + group, data = data_complete_cases_sensitivity_analysis[-28, ])

anova(m0_identified_regulation_SMS2, m1_identified_regulation_SMS2)
```

Adding whether BE and identified_regulation_SMS2 were completed during the same day or not as a predictor did not significantly alter the results.

:::

## Introjected regulation (SMS-2) and BEA validity analysis
Validity between introjected_regulation_SMS2 and BEA is investigated by correlation analysis. As both scales has undergone Rasch analysis, participants theta estimates (computed with weighted likelihood estimation - WLE) will be correlated, and since thetas are interval data, Pearson's correlation is applied.

::: panel-tabset

### Prepring data

```{r}
#complete cases data frame for validity analyses

#removing missing values in relevant items for complete cases analysis
#only BE items and one item from the other scales in the bulls eye study
#is needed (in this case the SubjektivPrestation item) 
#this is because there are no missing values for the other scales 
#after the intervention study (Hockeystudien) participants have been removed
#therefore this data frame will work for all validity analyses 

items_validity_analyses <- c(
  "BE_Competition_recoded",
  "BE_Training_recoded",
  "BE_PreparationRecovery",
  "BE_Life",
  "SubjektivPrestation"
)

data_complete_cases <- bulls_eye_merged_superfinal_data[complete.cases(bulls_eye_merged_superfinal_data[, items_validity_analyses]), ]

#155 participants to begin with
#33 participants from the intervention study (Hockeystudien) were removed (did not complete any scale beside Bulls Eye)
#1 participant (not from the intervention study) who completed the other scales but not the dartboard in Bulls Eye (only other parts of BE) and were therefore removed
#results in a complete cases data frame with 121 participants 

nrow(data_complete_cases)
```

### Preparing item data frames

```{r}
#item data frames
BE_validity_analyses <- data_complete_cases[, c(
  "BE_Competition_recoded",
  "BE_Training_recoded",
  "BE_PreparationRecovery",
  "BE_Life"
)]

introjected_regulation_SMS2_validity_analyses <- data_complete_cases[, c(
  "SMS_2_1_recoded",
  "SMS_2_7_recoded",
  "SMS_2_16_revised_recoded"
)]

#extracting thetas
BE_thetas <- RIestThetas(BE_validity_analyses)

introjected_regulation_SMS2_thetas <- RIestThetas(introjected_regulation_SMS2_validity_analyses)

#adding thetas to the data frame
data_complete_cases$BE_thetas_WLE <- BE_thetas$WLE 
data_complete_cases$introjected_regulation_SMS2_thetas_WLE <- introjected_regulation_SMS2_thetas$WLE
```

### Outlier identification
Visual inspection of potential outliers was only conducted for BEA to have the same sub-sample across validity correlation analyses. One statistical outlier was detected and marked in red in the plot below. This participant was row 28 in the data frame and will be removed in the upcoming correlation.

```{r}
{
  plot(data_complete_cases$BE_thetas_WLE,
       main = "Index Plot of BE_thetas_WLE",
       ylab = "BE Theta",
       xlab = "Participant Index",
       pch = 20)
  abline(h = mean(data_complete_cases$BE_thetas_WLE), col = "blue", lty = 2)
  points(28, data_complete_cases$BE_thetas_WLE[28], col = "red", pch = 19)
}
```

### Correlation introjected_regulation_SMS2 and BEA

```{r}
#participant on row 28 is an outlier and therefore removed
correlation_BE_introjected_regulation_SMS2 <- cor_test(
  data_complete_cases[-28, ],
  x = "BE_thetas_WLE",
  y = "introjected_regulation_SMS2_thetas_WLE",
  method = "pearson"
)

print(correlation_BE_introjected_regulation_SMS2)

plot(correlation_BE_introjected_regulation_SMS2)
```

### Sensitivity analysis introjected_regulation_SMS2 and BEA, time latency
Some participants did not complete BEA and SMS-2 during the same day as intended. Therefore, a sensitivity analysis is conducted.

```{r}
#creating data frame with only participants that completed Bulls Eye and the other scales during the same day
#since 17 participants did not (has already been checked in a prior validity analysis), 104 participants will remain 
data_complete_cases_less_than_1day <- subset(data_complete_cases, time_latency_survey1_bulls_eye1_days < 1)
```

```{r}
#looking only at participants who completed Bulls Eye and the other scales during the same day (N = 104)

#sensitivity analysis introjected_regulation_SMS2 and BE
BE_validity_analyses_less1day <- data_complete_cases_less_than_1day[, c(
  "BE_Competition_recoded",
  "BE_Training_recoded",
  "BE_PreparationRecovery",
  "BE_Life"
)]

introjected_regulation_SMS2_validity_analyses_less1day <- data_complete_cases_less_than_1day[, c(
  "SMS_2_1_recoded",
  "SMS_2_7_recoded",
  "SMS_2_16_revised_recoded"
)]

#extracting thetas
BE_thetas_less1day <- RIestThetas(BE_validity_analyses_less1day)

introjected_regulation_SMS2_thetas_less1day <- RIestThetas(introjected_regulation_SMS2_validity_analyses_less1day)

#adding thetas to the data frame
data_complete_cases_less_than_1day$BE_thetas_less1day_WLE <- BE_thetas_less1day$WLE

data_complete_cases_less_than_1day$introjected_regulation_SMS2_thetas_less1day_WLE <- introjected_regulation_SMS2_thetas_less1day$WLE

#analysis only with participants completing Bulls Eye and SMS-2 the same day
#removing the outlier, now on row 20 in the data frame
correlation_BE_introjected_regulation_SMS2_less1day <- cor_test(
  data_complete_cases_less_than_1day[-20, ],
  x = "BE_thetas_less1day_WLE",
  y = "introjected_regulation_SMS2_thetas_less1day_WLE",
  method = "pearson"
)

print(correlation_BE_introjected_regulation_SMS2_less1day)
```

```{r}
#we can also check if there is a statistically significant difference 
#by adding same or different day as a predictor
#the outlier on row 28 in the data frame is removed
data_complete_cases_sensitivity_analysis <- data_complete_cases %>% 
  mutate(group = factor(ifelse(time_latency_survey1_bulls_eye1_days < 1,"same_day","different_day")))

m0_introjected_regulation_SMS2 <- lm(introjected_regulation_SMS2_thetas_WLE ~ BE_thetas_WLE, data = data_complete_cases_sensitivity_analysis[-28, ])

m1_introjected_regulation_SMS2 <- lm(introjected_regulation_SMS2_thetas_WLE ~ BE_thetas_WLE + group, data = data_complete_cases_sensitivity_analysis[-28, ])

anova(m0_introjected_regulation_SMS2, m1_introjected_regulation_SMS2)
```

Adding whether BE and introjected_regulation_SMS2 were completed during the same day or not as a predictor did not significantly alter the results.

:::

## Re-analysis of external_regulation_SMS2 recoded version 

Based on the analysis of the response categories and threshold locations, scale steps were merged and recoded so that each kept scale step had the highest response probability at some point on the person location scale, and also so that all threshold locations were in the right order for all items. Recoded items were given new names with the abbreviation "_recoded". 

::: panel-tabset

### Recoding response categories for external_regulation_SMS2

```{r}
#add recoded external_regulation_SMS2 items

bulls_eye_merged_superfinal_data <- bulls_eye_merged_superfinal_data %>%
  mutate(
    # Recoding SMS_2_5_revised (1+2)
    SMS_2_5_revised_recoded = recode(
      SMS_2_5_revised,
      `0` = 0,
      `1` = 1, `2` = 1,
      `3` = 2,
      `4` = 3
    ),
    # Recoding SMS_2_8_revised (2+3)
    SMS_2_8_revised_recoded = recode(
      SMS_2_8_revised,
      `0` = 0,
      `1` = 1,
      `2` = 2, `3` = 2,
      `4` = 3
    ),
    # Recoding SMS_2_15 (3+4; 5+6)
    SMS_2_15_recoded = recode(
      SMS_2_15,
      `0` = 0,
      `1` = 1,
      `2` = 2,
      `3` = 3, `4` = 3,
      `5` = 4, `6` = 4
    )
  )

```

## External regulation (SMS-2) and BEA validity analysis
Validity between external_regulation_SMS2 and BEA is investigated by correlation analysis. As both scales has undergone Rasch analysis, participants theta estimates (computed with weighted likelihood estimation - WLE) will be correlated, and since thetas are interval data, Pearson's correlation is applied.

::: panel-tabset

### Prepring data

```{r}
#complete cases data frame for validity analyses

#removing missing values in relevant items for complete cases analysis
#only BE items and one item from the other scales in the bulls eye study
#is needed (in this case the SubjektivPrestation item) 
#this is because there are no missing values for the other scales 
#after the intervention study (Hockeystudien) participants have been removed
#therefore this data frame will work for all validity analyses 

items_validity_analyses <- c(
  "BE_Competition_recoded",
  "BE_Training_recoded",
  "BE_PreparationRecovery",
  "BE_Life",
  "SubjektivPrestation"
)

data_complete_cases <- bulls_eye_merged_superfinal_data[complete.cases(bulls_eye_merged_superfinal_data[, items_validity_analyses]), ]

#155 participants to begin with
#33 participants from the intervention study (Hockeystudien) were removed (did not complete any scale beside Bulls Eye)
#1 participant (not from the intervention study) who completed the other scales but not the dartboard in Bulls Eye (only other parts of BE) and were therefore removed
#results in a complete cases data frame with 121 participants 

nrow(data_complete_cases)
```

### Preparing item data frames

```{r}
#item data frames
BE_validity_analyses <- data_complete_cases[, c(
  "BE_Competition_recoded",
  "BE_Training_recoded",
  "BE_PreparationRecovery",
  "BE_Life"
)]

external_regulation_SMS2_validity_analyses <- data_complete_cases[, c(
  "SMS_2_5_revised_recoded",
  "SMS_2_8_revised_recoded",
  "SMS_2_15_recoded"
)]

#extracting thetas
BE_thetas <- RIestThetas(BE_validity_analyses)

external_regulation_SMS2_thetas <- RIestThetas(external_regulation_SMS2_validity_analyses)

#adding thetas to the data frame
data_complete_cases$BE_thetas_WLE <- BE_thetas$WLE
data_complete_cases$external_regulation_SMS2_thetas_WLE <- external_regulation_SMS2_thetas$WLE
```

### Outlier identification
Visual inspection of potential outliers was only conducted for BEA to have the same sub-sample across validity correlation analyses. One statistical outlier was detected and marked in red in the plot below. This participant was row 28 in the data frame and will be removed in the upcoming correlation.

```{r}
{
  plot(data_complete_cases$BE_thetas_WLE,
       main = "Index Plot of BE_thetas_WLE",
       ylab = "BE Theta",
       xlab = "Participant Index",
       pch = 20)
  abline(h = mean(data_complete_cases$BE_thetas_WLE), col = "blue", lty = 2)
  points(28, data_complete_cases$BE_thetas_WLE[28], col = "red", pch = 19)
}
```

### Correlation external_regulation_SMS2 and BEA

```{r}
#participant on row 28 is an outlier and therefore removed
correlation_BE_external_regulation_SMS2 <- cor_test(
  data_complete_cases[-28, ],
  x = "BE_thetas_WLE",
  y = "external_regulation_SMS2_thetas_WLE",
  method = "pearson"
)

print(correlation_BE_external_regulation_SMS2)

plot(correlation_BE_external_regulation_SMS2)
```

### Sensitivity analysis external_regulation_SMS2 and BEA, time latency
Some participants did not complete BEA and SMS-2 during the same day as intended. Therefore, a sensitivity analysis is conducted.

```{r}
#creating data frame with only participants that completed Bulls Eye and the other scales during the same day
#since 17 participants did not (has already been checked in a prior validity analysis), 104 participants will remain 
data_complete_cases_less_than_1day <- subset(data_complete_cases, time_latency_survey1_bulls_eye1_days < 1)
```

```{r}
#looking only at participants who completed Bulls Eye and the other scales during the same day (N = 104)

#sensitivity analysis external_regulation_SMS2 and BE
BE_validity_analyses_less1day <- data_complete_cases_less_than_1day[, c(
  "BE_Competition_recoded",
  "BE_Training_recoded",
  "BE_PreparationRecovery",
  "BE_Life"
)]

external_regulation_SMS2_validity_analyses_less1day <- data_complete_cases_less_than_1day[, c(
  "SMS_2_5_revised_recoded",
  "SMS_2_8_revised_recoded",
  "SMS_2_15_recoded"
)]

#extracting thetas
BE_thetas_less1day <- RIestThetas(BE_validity_analyses_less1day)

external_regulation_SMS2_thetas_less1day <- RIestThetas(external_regulation_SMS2_validity_analyses_less1day)

#adding thetas to the data frame
data_complete_cases_less_than_1day$BE_thetas_less1day_WLE <- BE_thetas_less1day$WLE

data_complete_cases_less_than_1day$external_regulation_SMS2_thetas_less1day_WLE <- external_regulation_SMS2_thetas_less1day$WLE

#analysis only with participants completing Bulls Eye and SMS-2 the same day
#removing the outlier, now on row 20 in the data frame
correlation_BE_external_regulation_SMS2_less1day <- cor_test(
  data_complete_cases_less_than_1day[-20, ],
  x = "BE_thetas_less1day_WLE",
  y = "external_regulation_SMS2_thetas_less1day_WLE",
  method = "pearson"
)

print(correlation_BE_external_regulation_SMS2_less1day)
```

```{r}
#we can also check if there is a statistically significant difference 
#by adding same or different day as a predictor
#the outlier on row 28 in the data frame is removed
data_complete_cases_sensitivity_analysis <- data_complete_cases %>% 
  mutate(group = factor(ifelse(time_latency_survey1_bulls_eye1_days < 1,"same_day","different_day")))

m0_external_regulation_SMS2 <- lm(external_regulation_SMS2_thetas_WLE ~ BE_thetas_WLE, data = data_complete_cases_sensitivity_analysis[-28, ])

m1_external_regulation_SMS2 <- lm(external_regulation_SMS2_thetas_WLE ~ BE_thetas_WLE + group, data = data_complete_cases_sensitivity_analysis[-28, ])

anova(m0_external_regulation_SMS2, m1_external_regulation_SMS2)
```

Adding whether BE and external_regulation_SMS2 were completed during the same day or not as a predictor did not significantly alter the results.

:::

## Re-analysis of amotivated_regulation_SMS2 recoded version 

Based on the analysis of the response categories and threshold locations, scale steps were merged and recoded so that each kept scale step had the highest response probability at some point on the person location scale, and also so that all threshold locations were in the right order for all items. Recoded items were given new names with the abbreviation "_recoded". 

::: panel-tabset

### Recoding response categories for amotivated_regulation_SMS2

```{r}
#add recoded amotivated_regulation_SMS2 items

bulls_eye_merged_superfinal_data <- bulls_eye_merged_superfinal_data %>%
  mutate(
    # Recoding SMS_2_2 (4+5+6)
    SMS_2_2_recoded = recode(
      SMS_2_2,
      `0` = 0, 
      `1` = 1, 
      `2` = 2, 
      `3` = 3, 
      `4` = 4, `5` = 4, `6` = 4
    ),
    # Recoding SMS_2_10_revised (2+3; 4+5)
    SMS_2_10_revised_recoded = recode(
      SMS_2_10_revised,
      `0` = 0, 
      `1` = 1,
      `2` = 2, `3` = 2, 
      `4` = 3, `5` = 3
    ),
    # Recoding SMS_2_13_revised (3+4)
    SMS_2_13_revised_recoded = recode(
      SMS_2_13_revised,
      `0` = 0, 
      `1` = 1, 
      `2` = 2, 
      `3` = 3, `4` = 3
    ))

```

#creating data frame with only participants that completed Bulls Eye and the other scales during the same day
#since 17 participants did not (has already been checked in a prior validity analysis), 104 participants will remain 
data_complete_cases_less_than_1day <- subset(data_complete_cases, time_latency_survey1_bulls_eye1_days < 1)
```

```{r}
#looking only at participants who completed Bulls Eye and the other scales during the same day (N = 104)

#sensitivity analysis amotivated_regulation_SMS2 and BE
BE_validity_analyses_less1day <- data_complete_cases_less_than_1day[, c(
  "BE_Competition_recoded",
  "BE_Training_recoded",
  "BE_PreparationRecovery",
  "BE_Life"
)]

amotivated_regulation_SMS2_validity_analyses_less1day <- data_complete_cases_less_than_1day[, c(
  "SMS_2_2_recoded",
  "SMS_2_10_revised_recoded",
  "SMS_2_13_revised_recoded"
)]

#extracting thetas
BE_thetas_less1day <- RIestThetas(BE_validity_analyses_less1day)

amotivated_regulation_SMS2_thetas_less1day <- RIestThetas(amotivated_regulation_SMS2_validity_analyses_less1day)

#adding thetas to the data frame
data_complete_cases_less_than_1day$BE_thetas_less1day_WLE <- BE_thetas_less1day$WLE

data_complete_cases_less_than_1day$amotivated_regulation_SMS2_thetas_less1day_WLE <- amotivated_regulation_SMS2_thetas_less1day$WLE

#analysis only with participants completing Bulls Eye and SMS-2 the same day
#removing the outlier, now on row 20 in the data frame
correlation_BE_amotivated_regulation_SMS2_less1day <- cor_test(
  data_complete_cases_less_than_1day[-20, ],
  x = "BE_thetas_less1day_WLE",
  y = "amotivated_regulation_SMS2_thetas_less1day_WLE",
  method = "pearson"
)

print(correlation_BE_amotivated_regulation_SMS2_less1day)
```

```{r}
#we can also check if there is a statistically significant difference 
#by adding same or different day as a predictor 
#the outlier on row 28 in the data frame is removed
data_complete_cases_sensitivity_analysis <- data_complete_cases %>% 
  mutate(group = factor(ifelse(time_latency_survey1_bulls_eye1_days < 1,"same_day","different_day")))

m0_amotivated_regulation_SMS2 <- lm(amotivated_regulation_SMS2_thetas_WLE ~ BE_thetas_WLE, data = data_complete_cases_sensitivity_analysis[-28, ])

m1_amotivated_regulation_SMS2 <- lm(amotivated_regulation_SMS2_thetas_WLE ~ BE_thetas_WLE + group, data = data_complete_cases_sensitivity_analysis[-28, ])

anova(m0_amotivated_regulation_SMS2, m1_amotivated_regulation_SMS2)
```

Adding whether BE and amotivated_regulation_SMS2 were completed during the same day or not as a predictor did significantly alter the result. 

:::

## BEA and SMS-2 subscales: Partial correlations
Partial correlations were conducted to examine the association between BEA and SMS-2 sub-scales, while controlling for the shared variance among the sub-scales.  

::: panel-tabset

### Prepring data

```{r}
#complete cases data frame for validity analyses

#removing missing values in relevant items for complete cases analysis
#only BE items and one item from the other scales in the bulls eye study
#is needed (in this case the SubjektivPrestation item) 
#this is because there are no missing values for the other scales 
#after the intervention study (Hockeystudien) participants have been removed
#therefore this data frame will work for all validity analyses 

items_validity_analyses <- c(
  "BE_Competition_recoded",
  "BE_Training_recoded",
  "BE_PreparationRecovery",
  "BE_Life",
  "SubjektivPrestation"
)

data_complete_cases <- bulls_eye_merged_superfinal_data[complete.cases(bulls_eye_merged_superfinal_data[, items_validity_analyses]), ]

#155 participants to begin with
#33 participants from the intervention study (Hockeystudien) were removed (did not complete any scale beside Bulls Eye)
#1 participant (not from the intervention study) who completed the other scales but not the dartboard in Bulls Eye (only other parts of BE) and were therefore removed
#results in a complete cases data frame with 121 participants 

nrow(data_complete_cases)
```

### Preparing item data frames

```{r}
#item data frames
BE_validity_analyses <- data_complete_cases[, c(
  "BE_Competition_recoded",
  "BE_Training_recoded",
  "BE_PreparationRecovery",
  "BE_Life"
)]

intrinsic_regulation_SMS2_validity_analyses <- data_complete_cases[, c(
  "SMS_2_3_recoded",

  "SMS_2_17_recoded"
)]

integrated_regulation_SMS2_validity_analyses <- data_complete_cases[, c(
  "SMS_2_4_recoded",
  "SMS_2_11_recoded",
  "SMS_2_14_recoded"
)]

identified_regulation_SMS2_validity_analyses <- data_complete_cases[, c(
  "SMS_2_6",
  "SMS_2_12_recoded",
  "SMS_2_18_recoded"
)]

introjected_regulation_SMS2_validity_analyses <- data_complete_cases[, c(
  "SMS_2_1_recoded",
  "SMS_2_7_recoded",
  "SMS_2_16_revised_recoded"
)]

external_regulation_SMS2_validity_analyses <- data_complete_cases[, c(
  "SMS_2_5_revised_recoded",
  "SMS_2_8_revised_recoded",
  "SMS_2_15_recoded"
)]

amotivated_regulation_SMS2_validity_analyses <- data_complete_cases[, c(
  "SMS_2_2_recoded",
  "SMS_2_10_revised_recoded",
  "SMS_2_13_revised_recoded"
)]

#extracting thetas
BE_thetas <- RIestThetas(BE_validity_analyses)

intrinsic_regulation_SMS2_thetas <- RIestThetas(intrinsic_regulation_SMS2_validity_analyses)

integrated_regulation_SMS2_thetas <- RIestThetas(integrated_regulation_SMS2_validity_analyses)

identified_regulation_SMS2_thetas <- RIestThetas(identified_regulation_SMS2_validity_analyses)

introjected_regulation_SMS2_thetas <- RIestThetas(introjected_regulation_SMS2_validity_analyses)

external_regulation_SMS2_thetas <- RIestThetas(external_regulation_SMS2_validity_analyses)

#adding thetas to the data frame
data_complete_cases$BE_thetas_WLE <- BE_thetas$WLE 

data_complete_cases$intrinsic_regulation_SMS2_thetas_WLE <- intrinsic_regulation_SMS2_thetas$WLE

data_complete_cases$integrated_regulation_SMS2_thetas_WLE <- integrated_regulation_SMS2_thetas$WLE

data_complete_cases$identified_regulation_SMS2_thetas_WLE <- identified_regulation_SMS2_thetas$WLE

data_complete_cases$introjected_regulation_SMS2_thetas_WLE <- introjected_regulation_SMS2_thetas$WLE

```

### Outlier identification
Visual inspection of potential outliers was only conducted for BEA to have the same sub-sample across validity correlation analyses. One statistical outlier was detected and marked in red in the plot below. This participant was row 28 in the data frame and will be removed in the upcoming correlation.

```{r}
{
  plot(data_complete_cases$BE_thetas_WLE,
       main = "Index Plot of BE_thetas_WLE",
       ylab = "BE Theta",
       xlab = "Participant Index",
       pch = 20)
  abline(h = mean(data_complete_cases$BE_thetas_WLE), col = "blue", lty = 2)
  points(28, data_complete_cases$BE_thetas_WLE[28], col = "red", pch = 19)
}
```

### Partial correlations 

```{r}
#partial correlations
#participant on row 28 is an outlier and therefore removed
partial_corr_BE_SMS2_subscales <- correlation(
  data_complete_cases[-28, ],
  select = "BE_thetas_WLE",
  select2 = c("intrinsic_regulation_SMS2_thetas_WLE",
              "integrated_regulation_SMS2_thetas_WLE",
              "identified_regulation_SMS2_thetas_WLE",
              "introjected_regulation_SMS2_thetas_WLE",
              "external_regulation_SMS2_thetas_WLE",
              "amotivated_regulation_SMS2_thetas_WLE"),
  partial = TRUE
)

print(partial_corr_BE_SMS2_subscales)
```
